b2-153.title: Kings and dictators
b2-153.story: Anna and Max visit the history museum in Kyiv for a school project. The first hall shows a portrait of a Russian [[tsar]] sitting proudly on his golden [[throne]]. Max jokes that he would rather be a medieval [[lord]] with a quiet castle and a big library. In the next room, the mood changes completely. A guide explains how a [[dictator]] used [[propaganda]] on radio and posters to control what people believed. Anna reads about a young [[fascist]] who later deeply regretted joining the movement. Another display tells the story of a brave [[dissident]] who spent years in prison for writing poems. The last hall is about the [[Holocaust|holocaust]], and everyone walks through it in silence. Outside, Max admits that history feels much closer than he expected. Anna nods and decides to write her project about courage and free speech.

b2-154.title: A history lecture
b2-154.story: On Thursday evening, Anna and Lisa go to an open lecture at the university. The guest speaker is an [[ex-president]] of a small European country, and the hall is packed. He is a skilled [[orator]], so even the difficult topics never feel boring. He starts with medieval [[scholasticism]], when scholars tried to explain faith through logic. Then he describes how a Renaissance [[humanist]] put human reason at the center of everything. Later, he warns how quickly [[Nazism]] spread in the 1930s, when people stopped asking questions. To finish, he shows a photo of an ancient [[pagoda]] in Japan that survived wars and earthquakes. "Ideas, like buildings, last only when people take care of them," he says. Lisa whispers that she finally understands why Anna loves history so much.

b2-155.title: Homework for every subject
b2-155.story: On Sunday, Taras asks Anna to help with his homework, which seems to cover every subject. First, he has to draw a [[pentagon]] and count the lines that connect its corners. Anna shows him how to draw a [[diagonal]] from one corner to another. Next comes English: he must find the [[imperative]] in the sentence "Open your book." Then he has to add an [[apostrophe]] to the words "dont" and "cant." For physics, Dad's old [[barometer]] on the wall suddenly becomes useful, because the needle is falling fast. Taras learns that electric current is measured in [[amperes|ampere]], while the kettle uses about two [[kilowatts|kilowatt]]. Finally, Dad brings a [[micrometer]] from his toolbox, and Taras measures the thickness of a single hair. "This is the best homework ever," he says, just as the rain begins.

b2-156.title: The science museum
b2-156.story: On a rainy Saturday, Max takes his sister Sofia to the new science museum. At the entrance, a huge [[multimedia]] screen plays videos about our planet. Sofia stops in front of a real spacesuit once worn by a [[cosmonaut]]. In the next hall, an old [[microcomputer]] sits beside a photo of a modern [[supercomputer]] that fills a whole room. A guide explains that the big machine helps scientists predict the weather for the entire country. Then they walk through a cold, dark room that copies the Arctic [[tundra]], with recorded wind and tiny plants. The last exhibit is a map showing how the Indian [[subcontinent]] slowly crashed into Asia. Sofia begs to stay until closing time. On the way home, she announces that she is going to be a scientist, or maybe an astronaut.

c1-01.title: A trendy café
c1-01.story: Ira has been dying to try a new fusion café in Podil, so she drags Anna along on Friday. The [[hostess]], her hair styled [[a la]] a 1960s film star, leads them to a tiny table by the window. Nearly every other seat is taken by a [[hipster]] hunched over a laptop and an oat-milk latte. The menu is ambitious: pork [[bao]], fettuccine [[alfredo]] with miso, and a cheesecake flavored with [[durian]]. Ira, a self-confessed food [[snob]], orders the cheesecake just to prove she's adventurous. Anna plays it safe with fresh [[grapefruit]] juice and a bowl of noodles. The moment the cheesecake arrives, its pungent smell drifts across half the room. Ira takes one heroic bite, smiles politely, and quietly slides the plate toward Anna. They leave laughing, agreeing that some trends are best admired from a distance.

c1-02.title: Backyard party
c1-02.story: Anna's dad decides to host a backyard party for the whole family on the first warm Saturday of June. He rolls out the grill, connects the [[propane]] tank, and spends ten minutes fiddling with the [[regulator]] until the flame finally steadies. Max shows up with a [[keg]] of homemade lemonade, which Taras immediately claims as his personal responsibility. Grandpa opens a bottle of [[pinot noir]] for the adults and lectures everyone on its subtle cherry notes. Meanwhile, Mama melts thick slices of [[cheddar]] over the burgers. Just as the food is ready, clouds roll in and everyone retreats indoors with plates piled high. Grandma declares that burgers eaten on the sofa are the ultimate [[comfort food]] on a gloomy evening anyway. Nobody argues; they simply [[chill]] in the living room, listening to the rain and finishing the lemonade.

c1-03.title: Baking day
c1-03.story: On a snowy Sunday, Grandma invites Anna and Taras to spend the whole day baking with her. She starts with her famous apple pie, insisting that the crust only turns flaky if you use [[lard]] instead of butter. Next, Anna whisks eggs and sugar for a batch of delicate [[madeleines|madeleine]], adding a few drops of lemon [[extract]]. Meanwhile, Taras is in charge of the chocolate [[fudge]], which mostly means stirring the pot and tasting it every two minutes. For the grand finale, Grandma attempts a [[creme]] brulee, caramelizing the sugar on top with a tiny kitchen torch. Unable to resist, Taras decorates the leftover cupcakes with far too much pink [[icing]]. By evening, the kitchen is a disaster, but the table looks like a French bakery. Grandpa samples everything and announces that he is never leaving this house again.

c1-04.title: Finding a new apartment
c1-04.story: Anna and Ira are finally ready to rent a place together, so they meet a cheerful [[realtor]] on Monday morning. First she shows them a glamorous [[penthouse]] with a rooftop terrace, which is clearly far beyond their budget. The second option is a converted [[loft]] above an old factory, full of character but freezing cold. Ira points out that the single [[radiator]] under the window could hardly heat a closet. Next comes a modern [[condominium]] where the [[intercom]] is broken, so they wait outside for fifteen minutes. In the car, Anna jokes that they should give up and rent a wooden [[chalet]] in the Carpathians instead. Their last stop is a small house with faded blue [[siding]] and a crooked porch. Inside, though, the [[layout]] is perfect: two bright bedrooms, a cozy kitchen, and a balcony facing the park. They sign the lease that afternoon, already arguing about who gets the bigger room.
